checks.name: reviewed actual signed first primitive
checks.detail: Read every line of SignedThresholdDerivative and GammaSignedFace: the genuine hard Gaussian H2 test is disintegrated along a unit normal. Actual Gaussian quadratic moments provide L1 and a finite global primitive Lipschitz budget; local residual slack is supplied volume-AE without full-family independence.

checks.name: reviewed actual generic Gamma derivative transport
checks.detail: Read every line of GammaLocalDerivative: true auxiliary threshold AC plus invertible affine threshold transport pulls the actual ordinary-volume derivatives to Gamma-AE. Real one-coordinate threshold updates, primal measurability/L1, uniform Lipschitz domination divided by sigma and actual chain rule justify differentiation of the genuine Gamma average.

checks.name: reviewed nonparallel mixed differentiation only
checks.detail: Read MixedDerivative and MixedCoarea: second-coordinate differentiation requires the two actual selected normals to be nonparallel and distinct. The signed facet primitive is globally Lipschitz in that other threshold with its genuine inverse residual scale. No generic assertion of second differentiability is applied to parallel pairs; no distributional boundary term is dropped.

checks.name: reviewed actual signed test and soft derivative
checks.detail: The original H2 test remains signed through both soft offset derivatives. The actual(q+1)/h and(q+2)/h factors follow from the checked distinct-offset logistic derivative. Equality and uniqueness of the actual derivatives yield the exact mixed soft/coarea identity, without assuming it as a premise.

checks.name: reviewed exact Gram and angle cancellation
checks.detail: Read all of GammaRidgeTrace: the actual orthonormal pair-section kernel has the true inverse square-root Gram factor. Multiplication by angle times sine cancels it exactly, leaving the literal native hardGaussianSignedRidgeTerm with every remaining hard constraint.

checks.name: reviewed parallel and diagonal cases
checks.detail: Unit parallel or antiparallel normals have sine zero, so the actual angle weight is zero pointwise. Their native signed ridge term is definitionally zero. The final all-ordered-pair identity includes these zero cases without invoking mixed Gamma differentiation there.

checks.name: reviewed honest finite-pair L1 and normalization
checks.detail: Actual H2 Gaussian polynomial domination proves every soft pair L1; the angle-weighted native signed ridge term has a genuine finite Gaussian density budget. Those bounds justify every finite-sum/Gamma interchange. Native Je is half the ordered-pair sum, so the exact resulting coefficient is2h²/((q+1)(q+2)sigma²), retained in the final theorem.

checks.name: reviewed precise final scope
checks.detail: The final signedRidge_soft_sum_coarea identity assumes only actual unit normal families, h>0, sigma>0, thresholds/physical point and the real Gamma shape index. No full-family linear independence, threshold slack, hard trace bound, base concentration or pair matrix estimate is an input. Those quantitative trace and matrix assemblies are separate downstream work.
